licence.note: The Apostles’ Creed is an ancient formula without an individual author; its received form is attested by the eighth century. It is in the public domain. This edition reproduces the Latin text as printed by Philip Schaff in 1877 (Schaff died in 1893) and only that: the editor’s Greek column, English translation, footnotes and introductions are not included.
licence.noteRo: Simbolul Apostolilor este o formulă veche, fără un autor individual; forma sa primită este atestată încă din secolul al VIII-lea. Este în domeniul public. Ediția reproduce textul latin așa cum l-a tipărit Philip Schaff în 1877 (Schaff a murit în 1893) și numai pe acesta: coloana grecească, traducerea engleză, notele de subsol și introducerile editorului nu sunt incluse.

provenance.source: Philip Schaff, The Creeds of Christendom, with a History and Critical Notes, vol. II, The Greek and Latin Creeds, with Translations (New York: Harper & Brothers, 1877; sixth edition), section I, Symbolum Apostolicum, (a) Forma recepta, p. 45: the Latin column only. Schaff took the text from the Psalterium Graecum et Romanum that James Ussher published (London, 1647); it agrees with the creed of Pirminius (d. 758). Digital text: Christian Classics Ethereal Library, ccel.org/ccel/schaff/creeds2 (ThML, public domain), read against the page text of the 1919 printing (Internet Archive, bibliothecasymbo020scha).
provenance.extractedBy: content/sources/symbolum-apostolorum/build-edition.ts: takes the text of the three Latin cells of the table in the ThML excerpt (markup and footnote markers removed), makes the one correction listed in SOURCE.md and cuts the text into twelve articles; the articles joined are the corrected text of the source, nothing is retyped. Ids by stableId.
provenance.notes: Twelve sections, one per article, with the headings 1 to 12, after the twelve articles of the Roman Catechism (1566); the division is an editorial layer, other counts of twelve exist, and it changes nothing in the text. Spelling and punctuation are Schaff’s (cæli, Jesum, ejus, judicare; descendit ad inferna, where other Latin copies read ad inferos). Schaff prints the est of inde venturus est in parentheses; the parentheses are removed and the word is kept. Not part of the edition: Schaff’s Greek column and English translation, footnotes and introductions. Not collated with a manuscript or a critical edition and not yet read by a philologist. issuingBody (the work has no individual author): the Western Church (labelEn "The Western Church", labelRo "Biserica apuseană", no year); the author record above stands for it until the catalogue carries the issuing body (the work schema has no field for it; docs/ui-spec-v2.md, 6.8). Record of the sources: content/sources/symbolum-apostolorum/SOURCE.md.
provenance.sourceDescription: The Latin of the received form of the Apostles’ Creed as printed by Philip Schaff in 1877, keyed in by the Christian Classics Ethereal Library and checked here against the page text of the printed book; cut into twelve articles. Not collated with a critical edition.

paragraphs.text: Credo in Deum Patrem omnipotentem; Creatorem cæli et terræ.
Et in Jesum Christum, Filium ejus unicum, Dominum nostrum;
qui conceptus est de Spiritu Sancto, natus ex Maria virgine;
passus sub Pontio Pilato, crucifixus, mortuus, et sepultus;
descendit ad inferna; tertia die resurrexit a mortuis;
ascendit ad cælos; sedet ad dexteram Dei Patris omnipotentis;
inde venturus est judicare vivos et mortuos.
